title: Beste meneer De Vries
subtitle: Emails and polite requests
intro: In this lesson you learn to write short emails in Dutch: formal ones to a manager and informal ones to a colleague. You practise polite requests with zou/zouden and the standard openings and closings. By the end you can move or confirm an appointment, send an attachment and reply politely.

words.note: The hyphen is normal in Dutch: de e-mail.

grammar.title: Polite requests with zou / zouden
grammar.explanation: Use **Zou u ... kunnen + infinitive?** for a very polite request. Use **Ik zou graag ... willen + infinitive** to say what you would like. **Zou** is for ik, jij, u, hij/zij/het; **zouden** is for wij, jullie and plural zij (they). The main verb (infinitive) goes at the very end.

rows: Zou u de afspraak kunnen verzetten?
Ik zou graag de afspraak willen verzetten.

grammar.tip: Start with Zou u ...? for a very polite request. For a wish, use Ik zou graag ... willen + infinitive.

grammar.title: Formal and informal emails
grammar.explanation: A formal email starts with **Geachte heer/mevrouw + surname** or **Beste meneer/mevrouw + surname**. Close with **Met vriendelijke groet,** + your name. An informal email starts with **Hoi + first name** or **Beste + first name**, and closes with **Groetjes,** + your name. Use **u** in formal emails and **je** in informal emails.

grammar.tip: In Dutch emails, the greeting is short. Give the reason for your email in the first sentence.

dialogue.title: Een e-mail en een berichtje
dialogue.setting: Sanne wants to move tomorrow's meeting with her manager, meneer De Vries, and then sends a quick message to her colleague Lisa.

lines.en: Dear Mr De Vries, unfortunately I cannot come to the meeting tomorrow.

lines.speaker: Sanne
lines.nl: Zou u de vergadering naar vrijdag kunnen verzetten?
lines.en: Could you move the meeting to Friday?

lines.speaker: Meneer De Vries
lines.nl: Beste Sanne, vrijdag om tien uur is goed.
lines.en: Dear Sanne, Friday at ten is fine.

lines.speaker: Meneer De Vries
lines.nl: Ik stuur u vandaag de informatie voor het project.
lines.en: I will send you the project information today.

lines.speaker: Sanne
lines.nl: Dank u wel. Ik reageer vandaag op uw bericht.
lines.en: Thank you. I will respond to your message today.

lines.speaker: Sanne
lines.nl: Hoi Lisa, ik stuur je de bijlage morgen.
lines.en: Hi Lisa, I will send you the attachment tomorrow.

lines.speaker: Lisa
lines.nl: Hoi Sanne, ik moet de bijlage vandaag hebben. Kan dat?
lines.en: Hi Sanne, I need the attachment today. Is that possible?

lines.speaker: Sanne
lines.nl: Ja, dat kan. Ik verstuur hem vandaag.
lines.en: Yes, that is possible. I will send it today.

lines.speaker: Lisa
lines.en: Thanks in advance! Best wishes, Lisa

culture.title: Dutch emails: short and direct
culture.text: In Dutch emails, the greeting is usually short. After 'Beste meneer De Vries,' or 'Hoi Lisa,' the writer often gives the reason for the email in the first sentence. Geachte is very formal and is mainly used in official letters or to people you do not know. In many workplaces, colleagues use je in everyday email, even when they use u in more formal situations.

summary: Use 'Zou u ... kunnen + infinitive?' for a very polite request.
Use 'Ik zou graag ... willen + infinitive' to say what you would like.
Formal email: Geachte heer/mevrouw ... or Beste meneer/mevrouw ...; close with Met vriendelijke groet, + your name.
Informal email: Hoi/Beste + first name; close with Groetjes, + your name.
Keep the greeting short and give the reason for your email in the first sentence.
